record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Make substantially better contact between constructive field theory and the C*-algebra or algebraic-field-theory approach, including the renormalization-group viewpoint in that setting.

evidence.quote: Make better contact with the C∗-algebra approach (sometimes called axiomatic field theory). We refer to [BV] for a point of view on the renormalization group in algebraic field theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Constructive quantum field theory (CQFT) aims to rigorously construct interacting quantum field theory models (e.g. P(φ)_2, φ^4_3, Gross–Neveu_2, etc.) typically via Euclidean functional integrals, cluster/multiscale expansions, and Wilsonian renormalization-group (RG) flows, ultimately producing Wightman functions satisfying the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms. The algebraic (or C*-algebraic / axiomatic) approach to quantum field theory (AQFT), in the sense of Haag–Kastler, instead specifies a theory by a net O ↦ A(O) of C*-algebras (or von Neumann algebras) on bounded regions O of Minkowski (or Euclidean) spacetime, satisfying isotony, locality (microcausality), covariance under the Poincaré group, and the spectrum condition. The renormalization-group viewpoint inside AQFT has been formulated, for instance, via scaling limits of nets of local algebras (Buchholz–Verch) and via perturbative algebraic quantum field theory (Brunetti–Dütsch–Fredenhagen).

Problem. Develop a substantive bridge between the constructive and the algebraic/C*-algebraic frameworks for interacting quantum field theory. Concretely, carry out the following:

(a) For a non-trivial interacting model rigorously constructed in CQFT (such as P(φ)_2 or φ^4_3), produce from the constructive data a Haag–Kastler net O ↦ A(O) of C*-algebras (or von Neumann algebras) satisfying isotony, locality, covariance, and the spectrum condition, and prove that the GNS vacuum representation reproduces the constructively built Wightman/Schwinger functions.

(b) Formulate the Wilsonian / multiscale renormalization-group transformations used in CQFT as a flow on a suitable space of nets (or of states on a scaling algebra) compatible with the Buchholz–Verch scaling-limit construction and with the Stueckelberg–Petermann RG of perturbative AQFT, and prove that the constructive RG fixed-point and stable manifold correspond to well-defined algebraic objects in this setting.

(c) Identify obstructions, or otherwise establish equivalence, between the two notions of "the same model": the constructively constructed Borel-summable interacting theory and the algebraically defined net obtained from (a)–(b).
artifact.category_tag: constructive vs algebraic quantum field theory
artifact.status_search_result: The program of unifying constructive QFT with algebraic/C*-algebraic QFT and incorporating the renormalization group remains an active and largely open research direction. Partial progress exists: Buchholz–Verch's scaling-algebra approach to the RG in AQFT, perturbative AQFT (Brunetti–Dütsch–Fredenhagen, Rejzner), and the integrable-models / deformation program of Lechner and collaborators have constructed nontrivial AQFT nets. However, no general framework systematically converts constructive multiscale-RG results (e.g. for φ^4_3) into Haag–Kastler nets and back, and surveys continue to list this as an open program.

status_evidence.title: Perturbative Algebraic Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the renormalization-group viewpoint within perturbative algebraic QFT, relating Stueckelberg–Petermann and Wilsonian RG.
status_evidence.claim: There is an established RG framework inside algebraic QFT, but it is perturbative and not directly tied to nonperturbative constructive models.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Constructive Quantum Field Theory: Integrable Models and Deformation Techniques
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys algebraic constructions of interacting nets via deformation/integrable-model techniques; describes the program of constructing AQFT models as 'still in its infancy'.
status_evidence.claim: Constructing AQFT nets corresponding to interacting models is ongoing and incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Constructive quantum field theory (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that examples in constructive QFT fall within the AQFT framework of Haag–Kastler, but the explicit bridge for rigorously constructed models is not generally available.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between CQFT models and Haag–Kastler nets is recognized but not fully developed.
